solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Funny company host entertaining one

indicators.note: to entertain a guest is to have them inside your house, so one letter goes within the host's letters

parts.note: an MC (master of ceremonies) hosts an event
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: A comedy firm's compere keeps a guest amused.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Funny company' reads as a comic troupe, but 'Funny' alone is the definition; MC is master of ceremonies.
explanation.definitionFit: A comic thing is amusing and makes people laugh, an adjective synonym.

clue.text: Porter maybe for an old king

definitions.meaning: ... Porter was the American songwriter, so Porter is one example of a person with this first name
Old King ... is the merry old soul of the nursery rhyme

explanation.surface: A railway porter is perhaps working for an aged monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Porter' looks like a luggage carrier; it is the songwriter Cole Porter.
explanation.definitionFit: Cole is the composer's given name and the nursery-rhyme monarch's name.

clue.text: Old bird beginning to twitch in ditch

parts.note: the moa was a giant flightless New Zealand bird, now extinct

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter, so only the start of twitch is used

explanation.surface: An ancient bird starts to twitch while lying in a ditch.
explanation.definitionFit: A moat is a water-filled trench around a castle, a kind of defensive channel.

clue.text: Officer studies information systematically displayed

parts.note: to con is an old word meaning to study or pore over, so studies gives cons
a table sets out data in rows and columns

explanation.surface: An official pores over data laid out in an orderly way.
explanation.definitionFit: A constable is a police officer of the lowest rank in Britain.

clue.text: Duck in river in Italy and river in African country

parts.note: the Po is Italy's longest river

indicators.note: one thing being in another places its letters inside, so the short letter goes within the country

parts.note: Chad is a landlocked country in central Africa
R is the usual abbreviation for river on maps

explanation.surface: A duck swims in an Italian river and in another river in Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: Three 'in's: the first is a link, the second sits inside the leaf for the Italian river, the third signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: The pochard is a diving duck found across Europe, so a duck species.

clue.text: Robber is quiet and angry

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning quietly
irate means angry

explanation.surface: A thief is described as silent and furious.
explanation.definitionFit: A pirate is a robber at sea, a specific kind of thief.

clue.text: Drink that's part of each afternoon

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a short run of letters inside the following words

explanation.surface: A beverage taken every afternoon.
explanation.definitionFit: Cha (or char) is British slang for tea, a beverage.

clue.text: First lady to occupy chair, unusually successful person

indicators.note: occupying a space means sitting within it, so one piece goes inside the other
doing something unusually means not the normal way, so the letters of chair are rearranged

parts.note: in the Bible Eve was the first woman

explanation.surface: The first woman takes the chair, an unusual success story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First lady' suggests a president's wife; here it is the Bible's first woman. 'unusually' is the anagram signal, 'to occupy' the container.
explanation.definitionFit: An achiever is someone who accomplishes goals, i.e. a winner in life.

clue.text: Somewhat elegant hands ruined with DIY

indicators.note: something ruined is wrecked and broken up, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Fancy-looking hands are spoiled by home improvement jobs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruined' rearranges HANDS and DIY (do-it-yourself home repairs).
explanation.definitionFit: A dandy is a man fussy about fine clothes; the -ish ending makes it rather stylish.

clue.text: Student not so thick, having embraced reading?

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold in your arms, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: leaner means thinner, less fat
R is one of the three Rs: reading, writing and arithmetic

explanation.surface: A pupil who is less dim, thanks to taking up books?
explanation.walkthrough: 'having embraced' puts R inside LEANER. 'Thick' looks like 'stupid'; here it means fat.
explanation.definitionFit: A learner is a pupil, anyone acquiring knowledge.

clue.text: A November in which female sits looking poorly?

indicators.note: in which, with the woman sitting there, says she is placed within the previous item

parts.note: N is November in the NATO phonetic alphabet
she is the female pronoun

explanation.surface: A November day in which a woman sits feeling under the weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in which … sits' puts SHE inside N, after A.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashen means pale as ash, as someone unwell looks.

clue.text: A tiny store specially designed for office materials

indicators.note: something specially designed is made up anew, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A small shop is purpose-built for selling office supplies.
explanation.definitionFit: Stationery means writing paper, pens and similar supplies used at desks.

clue.text: Old boy's meeting priest on street, becoming most vague

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil; with the 's added it gives OBS
a curé is a French parish priest

explanation.surface: A former pupil meets a priest in the street and grows hazier.
explanation.definitionFit: Obscure means unclear, so its superlative is the least clear of all.

clue.text: Together at home, having met up — and inside!

parts.note: being in means being at home

indicators.note: inside says the second word goes within the first
in a down clue up means read from bottom to top, so the word met runs backwards

explanation.surface: A couple at home after meeting up, and staying indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'met up' reads as gathering; 'up' reverses the word in a down clue, and 'inside' puts 'and' within, making TANDEM.
explanation.definitionFit: In tandem means working jointly or side by side, an idiom for jointly.

clue.text: Upset player given recognition and measured

parts.note: a cap is a player picked for a national team, recognised by being awarded a cap
sized means measured for size

explanation.surface: A sportsman, honoured and measured, is unsettled.
explanation.definitionFit: A capsized boat is overturned, and upset can mean knocked over.

clue.text: Bear running loose in New York right behind you!

indicators.note: in says the scrambled letters sit within the abbreviation
running loose suggests wild disorder, so the letters of bear are rearranged

explanation.surface: A bear escaped in New York is right on your heels!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bear' looks like the animal at large; 'running loose' is the anagram signal and 'in' the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Something nearby is close at hand, and right behind you is just that close.

clue.text: Flowers contributing to Easter Sunday

indicators.note: contributing to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Blooms brought along to decorate for Easter Sunday.
explanation.definitionFit: Asters are daisy-like garden plants, examples of blooms.

clue.text: A piece of cake? It may need a bit more than that!

definitions.text: A piece of cake? It may need a bit more than that!

parts.words: A piece of cake? It may need a bit more than that!
parts.note: a piece of cake means an easy task, as does the answer; but an outdoor meal needs more food than just one slice

explanation.surface: Something easy? It might take a little more effort.
explanation.walkthrough: Both 'piece of cake' and the answer are idioms for an easy job, and the outdoor meal would need more than cake.
explanation.definitionFit: An outdoor meal of packed food, and also an idiom for an easy thing.

clue.text: Sober? I assume half of bottle drunk

indicators.note: drunk means reeling and disordered, so these letters are rearranged
half of a six-letter word is its first three letters

explanation.surface: Is that sober? I suppose half the bottle has gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half of' takes BOT; 'drunk' rearranges it with I ASSUME.
explanation.definitionFit: Abstemious means sparing with drink, which is a kind of temperance.

clue.text: Tribe about to take most of country

parts.note: C is short for circa, Latin for about

indicators.note: most of means all but the last letter is used

parts.note: land means a country

explanation.surface: A tribe is set to seize most of a nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' drops the D from LAND.
explanation.definitionFit: A clan is a group of related families, a tribal kin group.

clue.text: Check uranium has been removed from passage

indicators.note: removed from says one letter is taken out of the word for check

parts.note: an audit is a check of accounts
U is the chemical symbol for uranium

explanation.surface: An inspection finds the uranium was taken out of a corridor.
explanation.definitionFit: An adit is a horizontal entrance tunnel into a mine.

clue.text: Twelve practise meditation, possibly?

parts.note: to do something is to practise it
Zen is a school of Buddhism built on meditation

explanation.surface: Twelve people practise meditation, perhaps?
explanation.definitionFit: A dozen is the number of items in a set of a dozen eggs or rolls.

clue.text: Nothing to fix — article has been discarded

indicators.note: discarded means thrown away, so a letter is taken out

parts.note: to nail something is to fix it in place
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: There is nothing to repair, since an item was thrown out.
explanation.definitionFit: Nil means zero, as in a sports score of none.

clue.text: Requirement came first, making one annoyed

parts.note: a need is a requirement
led means was in front, came first in a race

explanation.surface: A need took priority, which irritated someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Needled means provoked or irritated, a verb sense of being pricked.

clue.text: Note feature of act

indicators.note: feature of asks what characterises the word that follows, so the answer is read as a description of that word

parts.note: read as an instruction, the answer names the centre letter of the word act, a feature of that word

explanation.surface: Take note of an aspect of the performance.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as wordplay: the C at the centre of ACT is that word's feature.
explanation.definitionFit: Middle C is the musical pitch at the centre of the piano keyboard.

clue.text: Belief in number of commandments from a world beyond

parts.note: Moses received ten commandments
ET is the extraterrestrial of the film, a being from another planet

explanation.surface: Faith in the Commandments from beyond this world.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenet is a principle or doctrine held as true.
